units.translation: having ships built of beams, dark-prowed
a man strong with the spear

where in M δορυσσόοις σαγαῖς [with spear-brandishing shields] is written with seven letters σσαγαῖς [the letters σσαγαῖς] in an erasure of five letters. If the second sigma of the word σαγαῖς [shields] had been written by the first hand, since the letter π [p] that follows, according to the almost constant practice of this and other old manuscripts, would have had to be written in one stroke with it, σαγαῖ σπύλαις [with shield and arms], which was not done. For the form of the letter is such that it is clear it was not joined to another letter. Therefore the ancient reading was δορυσσόοι σαγᾶι [with spear-brandishing shield], i.e. δορυσόῳ σαγᾷ [with spear-brandishing shield], which I have restored. That the scholiast interpreted the plural δορυσόοις σαγαῖς [with spear-brandishing shields] as ταῖς διὰ τῶν δοράτων σωζούσαις πανοπλίαις [the full armor that saves through spears] and πολεμικαῖς πανοπλίαις [warlike full armor] is of no importance, since these, like many other things, could have come from a later scholiast interpreting an interpolated reading.
I see the crowd of shield-bearing and spear-brandishing men
they appointed these my followers and spear-brandishers
ταῖς διὰ τῶν δοράτων σωζούσαις πανοπλίαις [the full armor that saves through spears]
he orders the spear-bearing attendants to lead
a gift of earth mixed with blood
an evil gift of evils to the evil
and a gift worthy of their evils
with the gift of the gods
she gives a birthday gift to Phoebus
you see Prometheus, the giver of fire to mortals
that I may not meet with slavery
how far apart are ruling and being a slave
Here too M has δούλειον [slavish], but δούλιον [slavish] in the other place in the apograph.
Since in the remaining places the meter either demands or allows δούλιος [slavish], it was consistent to restore δούλιος [slavish] also in those few places where M has δούλειος [slavish].
δούλιος [slavish] corrupted from βούλιος [willing], which see.
with slavish yokes (thus Aldus for δουλείοισι [slavish])
a slavish city (thus here too correctly corrected for δουλείαν [slavery])
to cast a slavish yoke upon Hellas
for no one willingly uses a slavish yoke
the divine remains in a slavish mind
for one must bear the slavish yoke
